correctness.rationale: The gradient g_i=f(i+1)−f(i) is exactly a zero-sum edge vector, and it evolves by the same nearest-neighbor cycle Markov generator Q. Any zero-sum g is a positive transport combination of dipoles e_i−e_j preserving weighted l1 cost, so it suffices to test all dipoles. The exact right derivative F_ij=−(2+a_ij)(w_i+w_j)+sum_{k!=i,j}w_k|a_ki−a_kj| is both necessary (positive F gives strict small-time increase) and sufficient (for h<1/3 Euler step exactly decreases weighted l1 on all dipoles; powers converge to e^{tQ}). Counting adjacent/distance-two/distance-three/four cases gives stated n<=5 inequalities and n=6 pair-sum S and distance-two condition. For n>=7, nonpositive distance-three dipole derivatives have total zero, forcing w_i+w_i+3=S; n=7 gives w_i=w_i+6 and hence equality; n>=8 distance-four analogue gives w_i+w_i+4=T, and cyclic constant consecutive difference forces all weights equal. I independently computed F from raw Qg, without using package gain formula, and exhaustively matched classification on exact integer profiles at n=3..9 with totals 64,256,243,729,2187,256,512, including stable hexagon. These finite profiles corroborate, but universal result rests on transport/Euler identities.
